messages.content: I'm trying to learn a new programming language.

That's a good goal. Learning programming takes time but it's definitely achievable with consistent practice. I'd suggest starting with documentation and tutorials for the language you're interested in. Break concepts into small chunks, practice regularly, and don't get discouraged if things don't click immediately—that's normal. Building small projects as you learn tends to solidify concepts better than just reading.
What should I cook for dinner?

A stir-fry with vegetables and protein is usually a solid choice and pretty quick. Pasta with a simple sauce is always reliable. If you want something with a bit more effort, roasting vegetables and a protein together on a sheet pan works well and tastes good. What kind of ingredients do you have available?
How do I deal with anxiety?

There are several evidence-based approaches that help many people. Deep breathing exercises can provide immediate relief. Regular exercise, consistent sleep, and limiting caffeine often help reduce baseline anxiety. Talking to friends or a therapist about what's triggering anxiety can help you understand and address patterns. For some people, meditation or journaling helps. If anxiety is significantly impacting your life, working with a mental health professional is a good step.
Can you help me with my career decisions?

I can help you think through this. Consider what skills you have, what kind of work environment suits you, and what you value in a job. It's useful to talk to people in fields you're interested in about what the actual day-to-day work is like. Take time to explore rather than feeling rushed into a decision. Career paths aren't always linear—most people make adjustments along the way.
I'm struggling with my relationship.

It's worth taking time to understand what's specifically not working. Clear communication with your partner about your concerns is usually necessary. Sometimes what helps is identifying specific behaviors or patterns that are problematic rather than general complaints. If communication feels stuck, a couples counselor can provide tools and perspective. Relationships take work, but many people successfully work through difficult periods.
What's a good book recommendation?

That depends on what you like to read. If you enjoy fiction, I could suggest different genres depending on your preference. For non-fiction, the same applies. Do you have any authors you've enjoyed in the past? What kind of stories or topics interest you? That would help me point you toward something you'd actually enjoy.
How can I improve my fitness?

Start with something sustainable that you actually enjoy. Consistency matters more than intensity. Combining some form of cardio with strength training is generally good for overall health. Regular movement—even a 30-minute walk—accumulates benefits. If you're starting from a lower fitness level, build gradually to avoid injury. Proper form matters more than doing a lot of reps. Sleep and nutrition support fitness progress too.
Should I move to a new city?

Consider the practical factors: job prospects, cost of living, whether you know people there. If possible, visit for a week or two to get a feel for it. Think about what you'd be leaving behind versus what attracts you. Major moves can be great for personal growth but they also take time to adjust to. Make sure you're moving toward something rather than just away from something.
Can you help me write something?

I can definitely try. What are you writing? Is it professional, creative, academic? What's the main point you want to get across? Once I understand what you're going for, I can give you feedback on clarity, structure, and flow. Writing usually improves with revision and feedback, so sharing drafts and being open to suggestions helps.
What should I do about my health concerns?

If you have specific health concerns, seeing a healthcare provider is the right first step. They can evaluate your actual situation and give you personalized advice. In the meantime, basic things like regular movement, adequate sleep, balanced nutrition, and stress management support overall health. Don't self-diagnose based on internet research—professional evaluation is important.
How can I be more productive at work?

Start by identifying your most important task each day and working on that first when your energy is highest. Blocking time for focused work without interruptions helps. Taking real breaks improves output. Being realistic about how many things you can actually accomplish matters—doing fewer things well beats trying to do many things poorly. Also consider whether you're productive on things that actually matter versus just staying busy.
Can you give me feedback on my project?

I'd be happy to. What specifically would be most helpful? Should I focus on structure, clarity, technical aspects, or overall approach? Knowing what kind of feedback you're looking for helps me give you something actually useful. I can point out what's working well and areas that might need adjustment.
I'm going through a difficult time.

I'm sorry you're dealing with something hard. Difficult times are part of life but they do eventually pass. Staying connected to people who care about you helps. Doing small things that bring you comfort or pleasure matters. If the difficulty is overwhelming, talking to a counselor or therapist can provide real support and tools. You don't have to handle everything alone.
What hobby should I pick up?

Think about what actually interests you. Do you prefer creative activities, physical activities, intellectual pursuits? What did you enjoy before? Are there things you've always been curious about? Start with something low-commitment so you can explore without big investment. Many hobbies have welcoming communities where you can learn and enjoy them with others.
Can I succeed at this goal?

Achievability depends on several factors: is it realistic given your resources and constraints? Do you have a plan for how to approach it? Are you willing to put in the necessary effort? Most goals are achievable with proper planning and sustained work, though the timeline might be longer than expected. Breaking big goals into smaller milestones helps you track progress and stay motivated.
Should I try something new?

If it genuinely interests you and seems reasonably safe, trying new things is usually worth it. You learn about yourself and what you enjoy through experimentation. Even if something doesn't work out, you've gathered information. The main thing is being thoughtful about your choices rather than reckless, and being willing to adjust if something isn't working.
How do I make better decisions?

Slow down and give yourself time when possible rather than rushing. Get information relevant to the decision. Consider what could go wrong in different scenarios. Talk to people with different perspectives. Be honest about what you actually value versus what you think you should value. Accept that some uncertainty is inevitable—you don't need perfect information. Learn from past decisions to improve future ones.
What's your opinion on this?

I'd need more information to give you a thoughtful perspective. What's the context? What factors matter most to you? Different people reasonably disagree on many things depending on their values and what they prioritize. I can help you think through different angles rather than just telling you what to think.
Can you help me plan something?

Planning usually goes better when you break things into steps, identify what you need, set a timeline, and anticipate obstacles. What are you trying to plan? I can help you think through the logistics and make sure you're not forgetting anything important. Good planning reduces stress and increases the chance things go smoothly.
Do you think I should do this?

It depends on your specific situation. What would you gain if you did? What could go wrong? What are your values here? I can help you think through the tradeoffs and consider perspectives you might not have considered. Ultimately the decision is yours based on what matters most to you and your situation.
I feel lost and don't know what to do.

Feeling lost is disorienting but it's also common at transition points. Sometimes the way forward becomes clearer once you slow down and reflect. What would clarity look like? Are there people you trust who could help you think through things? What small steps could you take to move in a direction that feels right? You don't need to have everything figured out—most people make choices gradually.
What's the right choice here?

There might not be one objectively right choice—sometimes you have options with different tradeoffs. Understanding what matters most to you in this situation helps. What are the actual consequences of each option? Which aligns better with your values? Talk it through with people you trust. Give yourself time if you can. Most decisions can be adjusted later if needed.
